🇷🇺🇺🇦🇺🇸🇰🇿🛢 Novorossiysk, There Air Defense, U.S. Worries On Oil Profits:
KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Ukrainian anti-ship missiles, jet-powered aerial drones and sea drones blitzed a major Russian naval base on the Black Sea coast in a “unique” nighttime operation, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Wednesday.
Cutting-edge drones developed by Kyiv since Russia invaded more than four years ago have repeatedly targeted Russian ships in the Black Sea, including warships and oil tankers. Both countries have Black Sea shorelines.
Ukraine’s uncrewed fleet has succeeded in limiting the movements of Russia’s once-dominant Black Sea navy, Kyiv officials say, in one of the country’s biggest feats of the war.
But Ukrainian officials reckon that Russian President Vladimir Putin is bent on prosecuting the invasion, despite his bigger army’s slow and costly progress on the battlefield and U.S. diplomatic efforts to find a settlement.
Putin is planning “an additional rapid mobilization of several hundred thousand Russians by the end of the year,” Zelenskyy said on social media late Tuesday, citing Ukrainian intel.
Those reports have also said recently that Russia is expanding production of ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones, both of which are hard for Ukrainian air defenses to counter.
Meanwhile, Ukraine is also trying to scale up its weapons manufacturing through agreements with partner countries, as both countries apparently plan to fight on.
The Ukrainian military “carried out a unique operation targeting the naval base in Novorossiysk — the last major stronghold of the Russian fleet in the Black Sea,” Zelenskyy said in a social media post.
The attack struck air defenses, piers and other port infrastructure in the Krasnodar region city, he added.
Krasnodar region Gov. Veniamin Kondratyev said that hundreds of Ukrainian drones attacked Novorossiysk, Anapa and Gelendzhik and the Temryuk district overnight.
Novorossiysk is also home to a key international oil terminal. The Grushovaya oil transshipment complex near Novorossiysk is one of the largest transshipment hubs in southern Russia for oil and petroleum products.
Last Feb, the U.S. State Department expressed its displeasure about Ukraine’s attacks on Novorossiysk, saying they have impacted U.S. oil interests in ⁠Kazakhstan.
The Caspian Pipeline Consortium operates a pipeline from the Caspian coast in northwest Kazakhstan to Novorossiysk. The pipeline handles much of the crude exports from three major Kazakh fields in which major U.S. energy companies, Chevron and ExxonMobil, have stakes.
In illegally annexed Crimea, air defenses downed 115 Ukrainian drones over Sevastopol overnight, the city’s Russia-appointed head said, adding that 10 apartment buildings and 25 private houses were damaged.
Russian air defenses downed more than 500 Ukrainian drones Moscow said.
In Novorossiysk, an eight-year old child was killed in the attack, and a person wounded when his house in the Temryuk region was hit later died in hospital, Kondratyev said. He added that 12 other people in the region were wounded.
Debris from downed drones fell on the territory of four industrial plants and 21 residential buildings, according to Kondratyev, but officials gave no details of any damage.
Meanwhile, Ukraine’s air force said Wednesday that Russia fired 138 long-range strike drones as well as an unspecified number of missiles at Ukraine during the night. Damage was recorded at 16 locations across the country, it said.
In the southern Kherson region of Ukraine, a large-scale Russian drone attack overnight killed two people and wounded two others, regional head Oleksandr Prokudin said Wednesday.
The attacks also destroyed a shopping mall in the southern Ukraine city of Zaporizhzhia.
---
However, U.S. leadership is pushing back, specifically Vance and Trump, as they are concerned about American companies' financial connections to Russia and Kazakhstan's oil trade. More in next post.

From the Black Sea to the Danube waterway, Russia’s forces have ramped-up hammering attacks on Ukraine’s naval assets, port infrastructure and logistics chains.
Precision strikes with long-range Geran-series seeker drones, Lancet loitering munitions and air-launched high-precision weapons have targeted vessels, fuel depots, warehouses and transshipment facilities used to move Western weapons, ammunition, equipment and fuel to Ukrainian troops.
On the Danube, strikes on the ports of Reni and Izmail have severed the flow of NATO military supplies arriving by barge from Romania’s Constanta.
🔴 Reni is hammered for its role as the headquarters of Ukraine's naval command, a primary entry point for military imports including fuel, equipment, ammunition, and UAV components transported via barges from Romania

Along the Black Sea, Russia’s barrage of fire has been equally devastating, hitting:

👉 Chernomorsk port: Fuel depots, military storage facilities, and cargo ships at berth carrying weapons and equipment
👉 Nikolayev / Ochakov area: Dry cargo ships loaded with military equipment, weapons warehouses, and a Ukrainian patrol boat escorting vessels with Western arms
In open Black Sea waters, multiple dry cargo ships and tugboats escorting weapon-laden vessels east and southeast of Odessa, as well as ships en route to Ukrainian ports have come under attack.
Each strike dismantles another link in the logistical chain connecting NATO weapons to Ukrainian forces, degrades Ukraine's military logistics and steadily strangles the enemy’s war machine.

🇮🇱 How unhinged, genocidal Israel spiraled to fit its own ‘crazy state’ profile
For decades, Israeli strategic thinkers wielded the concept of "crazy states" as a diagnostic tool to justify preemptive war, subversion, and even annihilation against adversaries. 
Today, that same diagnostic framework fits Israel itself far better.
Back in 1971, Israeli political strategist Yehezkel Dror laid out in his book "Crazy States" the criteria: 
🔶 aggressive pursuit of far-reaching goals harmful to others
🔶 radical and intense commitments to achieve those goals
🔶 adoption of a morally superior posture while grossly contradicting international norms
Dror's prototypical case study was Nazi Germany, but he applied the label liberally to Israel’s Arab and Palestinian opponents. 
Since then, Israel has come to embody every characteristic Dror warned about.
In the current Knesset, 63 members identify with what were originally extreme far-right positions on Israel's borders, and only 14 support a two-state solution (of those, ten are Arabs).
Public opinion has moved in tandem: far more Jewish Israelis now identify as right-wing, and that increasingly means open discrimination against Palestinian citizens, annexation, extrajudicial measures, and preference for military force over negotiation.
Escalation has gone through the roof:

🇮🇷🚀 Iranian swift missile recovery leaves Israeli leadership in shock
Israeli military and intelligence officials have been caught off guard by the speed at which Iran has restored its military capabilities following the 2026 war, according to the Jerusalem Post.
During the 40-day war in 2026, the US and Israel launched more than 30,000 strikes against approximately 2,600 military and industrial targets, vastly exceeding previous campaigns in both scale and intensity. Yet despite the scale of the damage, Israeli defense officials have privately acknowledged that Iran has managed to rebuild faster than anticipated.
🔴 Iran used bulldozers to clear access to underground missile facilities that had been sealed off but not destroyed. This allowed it to regain access to stored munitions and arsenals
🔴 More critically, Iranian officials have confirmed that new production is now resuming at a far greater speed than analysts had projected, almost returning to its previous pace
🔴 If Iran can sustain a production rate of 100 to 300 missiles per month, it could restore its arsenal levels by mid-2027
Despite IDF assurances that the situation remains under control, Israeli leadership is beginning to sense a strategic deadlock amid growing disagreements with the US, which has shown little appetite for further escalation.
Trump's administration's "peace rhetoric" is driven by a stark contrast with Iran: while Iran is surging production, US stockpiles are being depleted at an alarming rate.
➡️ Nearly half of the US Tomahawk cruise missile inventory has been expended
➡️ Patriot interceptor stocks have dropped from roughly 2,200 before the war to between 759 and 827, while THAAD interceptors have fallen from 452 to fewer than 278
➡️ Gulf allies have also warned that missile interceptor shortages could weaken their capacity to intercept Iranian missiles if they come under retaliatory fire following further American strikes
➡️ US Army leadership, including Chairman of the Joint Chiefs General Dan Caine, is raising alarms and pressing Trump to withdraw from the conflict
